title: Amazon Front-End Development Engineer
description: A representative Amazon frontend loop spanning coding, UI implementation, web architecture, Leadership Principles, and bar-raiser judgment.
sources_note: Representative structure based on publicly described Amazon technical and Leadership Principles interviews; actual loops vary by team, location, and level.

rounds.title: Coding and Problem Solving
rounds.purpose: Assess correct, maintainable code, data structures, testing, and clear problem solving.

rubric_dimensions.label: Approach
rubric_dimensions.description: Decomposes the problem and selects a suitable approach.

rubric_dimensions.label: Correctness
rubric_dimensions.description: Implements correct logic and handles edge cases.

rubric_dimensions.label: Code quality
rubric_dimensions.description: Produces readable, maintainable, testable code.

rubric_dimensions.label: Communication
rubric_dimensions.description: Explains decisions and responds to feedback.

rounds.title: Frontend Implementation
rounds.purpose: Assess component design, JavaScript and browser fundamentals, state, accessibility, testing, and practical UI trade-offs.

rubric_dimensions.label: Functionality
rubric_dimensions.description: Builds behavior that satisfies the requirements.

rubric_dimensions.label: Component design
rubric_dimensions.description: Uses clear state, data flow, and reusable boundaries.

rubric_dimensions.label: Quality
rubric_dimensions.description: Addresses accessibility, testing, errors, and maintainability.

rubric_dimensions.label: Trade-offs
rubric_dimensions.description: Explains practical browser and framework decisions.

rounds.title: Frontend System Design
rounds.purpose: Assess client architecture, API contracts, performance, accessibility, reliability, and scale.

rubric_dimensions.label: Requirements
rubric_dimensions.description: Clarifies users, constraints, and experience goals.

rubric_dimensions.label: Client architecture
rubric_dimensions.description: Designs maintainable client boundaries and data flow.

rubric_dimensions.label: Performance and reliability
rubric_dimensions.description: Handles latency, caching, failures, and observability.

rubric_dimensions.label: Trade-offs
rubric_dimensions.description: Makes justified product and engineering decisions.

rounds.title: Leadership Principles
rounds.purpose: Assess specific evidence of ownership, customer impact, judgment, learning, and measurable results.

rubric_dimensions.label: Specificity
rubric_dimensions.description: Provides concrete situations, actions, and outcomes.

rubric_dimensions.label: Ownership
rubric_dimensions.description: Shows clear personal responsibility and judgment.

rubric_dimensions.label: Customer impact
rubric_dimensions.description: Connects decisions to customer outcomes.

rubric_dimensions.label: Results and learning
rubric_dimensions.description: Quantifies results and reflects on learning.

rounds.title: Bar Raiser
rounds.purpose: Assess calibrated judgment, high standards, principled disagreement, and level-appropriate scope.

rubric_dimensions.label: Evidence
rubric_dimensions.description: Supports claims with detailed personal evidence.

rubric_dimensions.label: Judgment
rubric_dimensions.description: Balances speed, risk, data, and principles.

rubric_dimensions.label: High standards
rubric_dimensions.description: Raises quality and addresses root causes.

rubric_dimensions.label: Level scope
rubric_dimensions.description: Demonstrates influence and complexity appropriate to level.
